messages:
maya: Hey support, getting 401 invalid_api_key from our hosted requests since this morning. Repro steps below.

maya: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
maya: Response: {"error":"invalid_api_key","message":"API key is invalid or expired"}

sam: Can you paste the output of `echo "$REDWOOD_API_KEY"` (masked okay) or at least first/last 6 chars?

maya: Paste:```
ssh-rsa AAAAB3NzaC1yc2EAAAADAQABAAABAQCu...
```
maya: Doh — that's my SSH public key. I accidentally ran `export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$(ssh-add -L)"` when copying keys across.

julian: Ah that explains it. Redwood API keys are 32+ char tokens (often prefixed) and we validate format server-side, so an SSH pubkey will fail lookup and return 401.

sam: For mitigation, rotate the key from dashboard (or create a new one) and update the env var. In the meantime you can `unset REDWOOD_API_KEY` or stop the service until the correct value is set to avoid leaking the SSH key.

support-bot: Ticket #SUP-2093 created and assigned to infra.team. Added label: "malformed-key-copypaste". Docs suggested: https://docs.redwood.ai/api-keys#format

maya: Confirmed rotating the key fixed it, services responding again. Thanks.

julian: We'll add a short CLI/SDK guard to detect obviously wrong values (ssh- keys, long whitespace/newlines) and show a helpful error instead of silent 401. Filed RFC for a small validation check.

sam: Quick reg-ex we can use in the short-term: `^rsk_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{24,}$` — if it doesn't match, print guidance: "Looks like a non-API key (ssh key / cert). Please check your REDWOOD_API_KEY."

maya: Nice, thanks both — closing this thread.
